views.label: through the bounce
caption: The Kretschmann scalar $K$ of the radiation universe against $\rho$ through contraction and expansion ($a = 1$, $-1 \le act \le 1$), the same at every $\phi$ and $z$. $K$ rises at every fixed $\rho$ until the bounce at $t = 0$ and then falls, its radial profile changing shape as well as height. On the axis $K$ rises from $33.6a^4$ at $act = -1$ to $792a^4$ at the bounce, its global maximum, and returns to $33.6a^4$ at $act = 1$. The radiation has a traceless stress tensor, so the Ricci scalar vanishes.
views.settings: $a = 1$, so that $1/a$ is the unit of every length. The moments run in steps of $0.05$ in $act$.
views.clip: We draw $K/a^4$ on a logarithmic scale from $10^{-4}$ to $10^3$; every value drawn lies within it.

views.label: the plane of $ct$ and $\rho$
caption: The Kretschmann scalar $K$ of the radiation universe over the plane of $ct$ and $\rho$ ($a = 1$), the same at every $\phi$ and $z$. The curvature is finite through the bounce at $t = 0$, and is the same at $t$ and $-t$. At every moment $K$ falls outward from the regular axis, and at every radius it falls away from the bounce in either time direction. The radiation has a traceless stress tensor, so the Ricci scalar vanishes.

At fixed radius $K$ tends to zero as $\cosh^{-8}(act)$ far in the past and future. At fixed time it tends to zero as $\cosh^{-4}(3a\rho)$ far from the axis. The maximum $792a^4$ at $t = \rho = 0$ is finite.
views.settings: $a = 1$, so that $1/a$ is the unit of every length.
views.clip: We colour $K/a^4$ on a logarithmic scale from $10^{-4}$ to $10^3$, and give a value beyond it the colour of the end it passes. Every value in this window lies within it, from $0.00011a^4$ at $a\rho = 1$, $act = \pm 1$, to $792a^4$ at the bounce on the axis.
